caption:
Why does a ratchet only click one way? 🤔
Guess: how many teeth does this gear have? 👇
Follow @whyloop.hq for a new machine every day
#ratchet #howitworks #engineering #mechanism #tools
firstComment:
Answer: 24 teeth 🔧

Each tooth has a gentle slope on one side and a steep face on the other. A small spring pushes the orange pawl into the teeth.

Swing the handle one way: the pawl jams against a steep face, so the gear, the socket and the bolt turn with the handle.
Swing it back: the pawl rides up each gentle slope and snaps into the next gap. That snap is the click, and the gear doesn't move.

On most real ratchets a small lever on the head flips the pawl, so the same tool can tighten or loosen. Fine-tooth ratchets have more, smaller teeth, so you need a shorter swing before the pawl catches the next tooth.

(Simplified 3D model: 24 teeth and one pawl; the reversing lever is not shown.)

Sources: Wikipedia, "Ratchet (device)" and "Socket wrench".
altText: 3D animation of a ratchet wrench with its cover plate removed, sitting on a socket on a wooden workbench. Inside the head, an orange spring-loaded pawl rests against a 24-tooth sawtooth gear. When the handle swings one way, the pawl locks against a tooth and the gear turns with it. When it swings back, the gear stays still and the pawl slides over the teeth with two clicks. Text on screen: Why does it click one way? The pawl.
